newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Debt-ridden Gulf Air cuts jobs.
newsitem.headline: Debt-ridden Gulf Air cuts jobs.

text.p: Debt-ridden regional carrier Gulf Air is axing scores of employees to cut costs, Bahrain's Gulf Daily News newspaper reported on Thursday.

So far 40 staff -- 15 Bahrainis, 24 Omanis and a Qatari -- have received their dismissal letters, the daily quoted unnamed sources as saying. In addition, about 100 employees are being told to retire early, it added.
The airline said last month it expected staff cuts under a restructuring programme to help recover from heavy losses.
The Manama-based carrier, owned by the governments of Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and Abu Dhabi emirate in United Arab Emirates, posted a $159 million loss in 1995.
It has not yet announced its results for 1996.

Last year, Gulf Air began offering an early retirement programme for Bahraini staff who had served for at least 20 years. More than 70 staff are believed to have taken advantage of the programme, the paper said.
More dismissals of Bahraini staff are expected, with the total seen at between 80 and 110, the newspaper reported.
Officials have said the carrier faced $2 billion in debts resulting from lavish buying of costly aircraft on loans and opening numerous uneconomic routes in the 1980s.
